verses.text: This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD while Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and all its towns, with his whole army and all the kingdoms and peoples of the earth under his rule:

"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah. Tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am going to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.

You will not escape from him. You will certainly be captured and handed over to him. You will see the king of Babylon with your own eyes, and he will speak to you face to face. And you will go to Babylon.'
But listen to the LORD's message, Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what the LORD says about you: 'You will not die by the sword.

You will die in peace. As people burned spices in honor of your ancestors, the kings who came before you, so they will burn spices in your honor and mourn for you, saying, "Oh no, master!" I myself have promised this,' says the LORD."
Then Jeremiah the prophet told all this to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.
At the time, the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and the remaining towns of Judah, Lachish and Azekah. These were the only fortified towns left in Judah.
The LORD's message came to Jeremiah after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to announce freedom for the slaves.
Everyone was to set free their Hebrew slaves, both men and women. No one was to keep a fellow Jew as a slave.
All the officials and people who made this covenant agreed to set their male and female slaves free and not keep them as slaves any longer. They obeyed and let them go.
But later they changed their minds. They took back the slaves they had freed and forced them to become slaves again.
Then the LORD's message came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I made a covenant with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, the land where they were slaves. I said,

'At the end of every seven years, each of you must free any fellow Hebrew who has sold himself to you. After he has served you six years, you must let him go free.' But your ancestors did not listen to me or pay attention.
Recently you turned back and did what is right in my eyes. Each of you announced freedom for your fellow Hebrews. You even made a covenant before me in the temple that is called by my name.
But then you turned around and dishonored my name. Each of you took back the male and female slaves you had set free to go wherever they wanted. You forced them to become your slaves again."

"So this is what the LORD says: You have not obeyed me by announcing freedom for your fellow Hebrews and neighbors. So look, I am announcing freedom for you," says the LORD, "freedom to die by war, disease, and famine. I will make you something terrible to all the kingdoms of the earth.
I will hand over the people who broke my covenant and did not keep the terms of the covenant they made before me. They cut a calf in two and walked between its pieces.
The officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests, and all the people of the land walked between the pieces of the calf.
I will hand them over to their enemies who want to kill them. Their dead bodies will become food for the birds and the wild animals.
I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials to their enemies who want to kill them, to the army of the king of Babylon, which has pulled back from you for now.

Look, I will give the order," says the LORD, "and I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, capture it, and burn it down. I will make the towns of Judah a ruin where no one lives."
